Beyond that, the speaking voice had weird tone, pretty flat and unusual cadence. Context: I’m a native speaker, checking out the app for my non-Japanese speaking dad. Advised him against it.

reviews.title: Email kerfluffle
reviews.text:
Now 1 star. Ugh.

Two things about the app that are frustrating right now I’m hoping they can fix them both!

The first - if you sign up on their Instagram ad with one email, and it’s not the email in your credit card account, then the system has a problem letting you into the iOS app.

The second (which is arguably a more serious problem) is if you have completed some lessons and then log out and log back in… the system does NOT remember the lessons you completed to that point.

But wait - it gets worse. Never heard back about the “missing progress” info, so I decided to cancel.

I thought it canceled properly and we get a refund Such a day or so I asked where the refund was. I mean, it seems only fair: if you’re billing me at the start of a trial, when I cancel I want the money back.

So out of curiosity I wanted to see what the status was, and I assume after they confirmed my account information. They said if you canceled within 7 days, you should receive a credit in 3 to 5 days. It depends on your card/bank.

But for some reason, I had a bad feeling about this, because I realized after they should be able to see the date I canceled.

So I googled how to request a refund from these folks. Turns out it’s a separate page and login method to request a refund for the charge on your trial. I’m not gonna say it’s deceptive but the website where I first canceled really looked like I had canceled everything, but apparently that only canceled the renewal.

reviews.title: If this isn’t a scam, it’s scam-adjacent.
reviews.text:
I hadn’t been making very good progress on Duolingo, and after seeing a Facebook ad for Jumpspeak, I decided to sign up online. It was $79, which was expensive, but I figured it would motivate me. I should’ve gotten wary when I saw that—even after I spent nearly 80 bucks—the website immediately tried to get me to upgrade to “Premium” (for a lot more money, of course). So I came here and downloaded the app. What a letdown! The layout is confusing, not intuitive at all, and there’s very little direction about how to break it down into lessons. Worst of all, the vast majority of features and lessons have the little “lock”symbol, indicating that they’re for Premium users only, and the app still keeps trying to make you shell out extra money to upgrade. 
For $79, I expect a standalone educational app that doesn’t constantly try to sell me an upgrade and taunt me with sections I can’t even open without dropping another $150. There really should be two separate apps and the non-premium one should be worth the money.
Considering that Duolingo is free and much easier to use, this is a no-brainer. If they didn’t make it so difficult to cancel your subscription and get your money back, I would’ve deleted this worthless app already. Don’t waste your money.

reviews.title: App is a scam
reviews.text:
They claim to have a 100 day free trial but if you try to cancel they say the trial period is only 30 days. Then they will continue to bill your credit card after you cancel for future subscriptions. I wish I’d read trustpilot reviews before signing up to save myself the headache. Stay away.

Update after developer response: I contacted support and asked them to a refund. After several days of delays, I was met with responses that did not address my questions or concerns. The responses either came from bots or from agents who did not read English very well. Either way, none of my concerns were addressed. I asked my credit card for a chargeback.

reviews.title: Pros and cons
reviews.text:
I liked several things about Jumpspeak. It encourages you to actually speak, and the conversations felt much more like real-world situations than the disconnected vocabulary drills or unnatural practice sentences found in some language apps.

Unfortunately, the speech recognition became frustrating enough that I decided to cancel. The app often seemed to assess my pronunciation before I had finished speaking, or it would cut me off and then tell me I had not completed the word or phrase. That made practicing feel discouraging rather than helpful.

I was also disappointed with the cancellation experience. It was not easy to find a clear path to cancel, and I repeatedly ended up being directed between different pages. I eventually managed to cancel, but one of my refund requests was denied because I was just outside the 30-day refund period. They did honor the separate $69 refund that was covered by their 100-day guarantee, which I appreciate.

Given how easy it is for a free trial to convert to a paid subscription, I also think a reminder shortly before the trial ends would be a courteous feature, particularly when the cancellation process itself is not especially straightforward.

There are genuinely good ideas behind Jumpspeak, especially the emphasis on speaking and practical conversation, but the technical frustrations and cancellation experience outweighed the positives for me.

reviews.title: Great supplement!

reviews.title: Not effective and concerning payment policies
reviews.text: Would not recommend on both effectiveness and ethical practices. As others have mentioned, this is not the most effective language learning app out there (as a non-native English speaker who has another 3 languages under their belt). Additionally, as others have mentioned, the payment plan is very sketchy. I had no warning of my renewal, especially because the app had been inactive for so long. Not even an email receipt of the renewal, I was only able to see it when I checked my bank account. Because I don’t check my account every single day (who does outside of investing?!) I was only able to see the charge 3 days after, and when I requested a refund, they said the window was a struck 24 hours which is ridiculous. They then said (and I’m sure it’s what they’ll post as a response to this review) that their policy is labeled when you initially sign up, but there’s nothing stated regarding a warning that you will not receive any renewal notice. Ethically, the company could do much better (as most subscription services out there would have at least a week window to cancel and request a refund, especially for an app where they can track when you’ve logged in a actually used the product).

reviews.title: JUMPSPEAK IS A SCAM
reviews.text:
This app is one of the worst ever created. If you’re unfortunate enough to lend them your financial information, then you will have no choice but to cancel your card, otherwise you’ll be charged hundreds of dollars without recourse. Part of the ruse has to do with subscribing either through the app or the website. If you go directly through the website, you might have a chance to avoid being cheated, since there’s no third party for these criminals to hide behind. If you go through the app, they’ll refer you to a robot that plays dumb and it will be impossible to be treated fairly, since they can just blame the third party and refuse responsibility for their crimes. 

This absolute scam is part of a wave of criminal behavior within the online world where they will bait well meaning people to giving them money via a third party and then leave them with nothing. I have even met one of these people at a foot massage place in Southeast Asia and was taken aback at how shameless he was about these businesses practices; it was even creepier since he was rubbing his hands together the entire time he was speaking jovially about how the third party subscription trick made them enough money to refund all the website subscribers while paying for a reverse engineered Frankenstein app created in the basement of an abandoned 3 star hotel in rural Cambodia. Buyer beware!

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
I wanted to like Jumpspeak, but my experience left me disappointed.

I signed up for the 3-month plan expecting to be able to fully evaluate the app. Instead, I was repeatedly prompted to upgrade to the highest-priced tier. The app already represents a significant investment, and it continually pushed me toward an annual subscription.

The biggest frustration came when I tried to review lessons I had already completed. Rather than letting me revisit material, the app told me I had reached my daily quota and encouraged me to upgrade to the more expensive plan. In my opinion, being able to review completed exercises is a fundamental part of learning a language, not a premium luxury.

Another reason for my low rating is the refund experience. The app advertises that dissatisfied customers can receive a refund within the trial period. Because my purchase was processed through Apple, I had to request the refund through Apple, and my request was denied. That left me feeling caught between the developer’s advertised guarantee and the platform that handled the payment.

For me, the value simply wasn’t there. There are other language-learning resources available at a much lower cost that provide effective practice when used consistently.

This was my personal experience, and based on it, I cannot recommend Jumpspeak.

reviews.text: The experience with this learning app was decent but did not ultimately suit my needs. When I tried to cancel during the trial period, I found it trying to actually find the place where you could cancel was incredibly difficult to locate. After multiple attempts, the time ran out and I ended up being charged over $268. When I reached out to their customer service portal, all I was able to do was engage with their AI Chatbot. They refused to connect me with an actual person and now I'm just resigned to the fact that I am out this money. Please enter into this with eyes wide open before you test it out.

reviews.title: Slow response time
reviews.text: App has a very slow response time it also cannot hear or recognize my voice. I have to speak several times before it hears me. Also if keeps “falling asleep” when I’m using the app. I have to keep tapping it.

reviews.title: Not so good for Thai, beginner and maybe not Asian languages.
reviews.text:
The main issues I see have only been my limited experience of attempting to use for augmenting my Thai learning.  I am a native English speaker.  

1.  Thai specific: while the app lets you set your gender and the gender of the other person, the AI model doesn’t seem to understand that in Thai, the ka and krap endings relate to the speakers gender.

2. May only Apply to Thai and other alphabets that are not rooted in Latin.  The app gives helpful advice at the end of the conversation, but unfortunately, it quotes the foreign language in its native alphabet; this which assumes that the user can read and pronounce in that alphabet.  During the conversation, the questions and suggested answer have both the local alphabet spelling and the Latin character phonetic spellings.  Would be great to have both in the analysis.

reviews.title: Warning: scammy billing, underwhelming product
reviews.text: I should have read all the other reviews. These guys are sleazy. I paid for a “premium” subscription promising me conversation style language training. Then, I discover that that’s a whole other level of “AI premium” service, costing an additional $180, above and beyond original subscription.  They offer it for free to test. And then without any warning, they bill you for it. No opting in.  No communication. Just boom - another $180 siphoned from your credit card. All this for a pretty underwhelming product that I tried and quickly dismissed.  I’m submitting a fraud claim.

reviews.title: Terrible app
reviews.text: It’s terrible. And they hide the subscription as much as possible to make it impossible to cancel. And there is no human support, only a chat bot with limited answers and terrible performance.  Don’t use this app!!

reviews.title: Huge waste of money
reviews.text: I purchased this in joyful excitement as an alternative to Duolingo, as it promised so much more. The ability of this app to understand you speak in the “spoken” and “conversation” portions is ridiculously bad. There’s no access to any customer service. It’s definitely a “pay us and we don’t care after that” type of deal. I’d rate Duolingo a “C”, this gets as an “F-“

reviews.title: No different
reviews.text: This app is no different than any of the others. Their commercial say that Duolingo teaches you to press buttons. So does this. Matching words to pictures just like Rosetta Stone and babel. Absolutely not worth it. The lessons don’t make sense either. The box flashing “next” skips over lessons. This is not a good way to learn.

reviews.title: Immersive app
reviews.text:
I think this app is great for anyone wanting to learn any language, particularly the romantic languages which come a little bit easier such as a Spanish. Currently I'm trying to learn Turkish, and I'm starting to understand sentence structure just by doing a lot of the practice over and over each day. I think it helps to keep notes of various vocabulary in a small journal so that you don't forget it later and the act of writing it down and even color-coding actually helps with the memory part.

One thing I will say, sometimes the microphone doesn't pick up certain words that I'm saying very clearly, and sometimes it will also tell me that I fully pronounce the word when I only pronounced half of it. I don't know if this is something that needs to be reviewed by the developer? sometimes it's slow to pick up certain words too and I am trying to pronounce everything to the best of my ability.  but i'm going to stick with it and see where it takes me.

reviews.title: ILLEGAL SCAM
reviews.text: At renewal, they don’t tell you they are going to charge your method of payment or tell you that your method of payment has been charged. No receipt of payment. They are set up to steal your money until you notice.

reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.text: This may be a bit more money but I promise it is worth it. You have real conversations! Not just repeating all the time. There are exercises that span different learning styles too. It’s a great tool and my Dutch girlfriend gets so excited when I say things correctly! They HATE when you botch their language! Lol

reviews.title: AI slop and shady billing practices
reviews.text:
Update: I cancelled last year and have email confirmation, yet they continue to bill me. Absolute trash company 

Original review: I know some Japanese so I jumped in from the beginning to see how it would teach a beginner. There were so many mistakes (grammatical and functional with the app).

I switched to a language I didn’t know and not only did it start asking me to form sentences from words I hasn’t yet learned but the functional bugs were back as well and worse.

At one point it wanted me to form  the sentence “nihao nihao ma”, but it would only accept the “nihao” tiles in a certain order even though they were identical.

Just feels like someone used AI to build an app and did no testing.

reviews.title: Hola!
reviews.text: I’m so happy with this method. I committed to 10 minutes a day but find myself doing at least 20!

reviews.title: Won’t refund you -terrible customer service
reviews.text:
They don’t give you a heads up when your subscription is renewed. I noticed within 72 hours & they refused to refund me. 

Would never recommend based on this alone. A 24 hr policy with no notification of renewal?

reviews.title: Draw
reviews.text: This language app is perfect for a beginner. Absolutely perfect! I’m so happy I’m actually learning and having fun doing it.😜 Jumpspeak is amazing and by far the best👍🏾

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text: I did the free trial and cancelled way before the renewal date and I’m still getting charged multiple times. They make it as hard as possible to end the subscription and then continue to charge you even after you cancel.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: Seriously disappointed. When given a sentence to translate, if it’s incorrect no help is given. Getting to a help screen is also difficult. Do not recommend   Oh, it really sucks. Can’t even post a review because apparently all the words I know are “taken”

reviews.title: This app sucks.
reviews.text: Very user unfriendly…the MMI for the mobile app is pretty much impossible to use. Maybe they’re still working out the bugs; but it’s unusable in its current format.  Apparently the customer service sucks too, judging from all the other reviews.
